statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r is the maximum cardinality of a finite set S of integers such that: every x in S satisfies 1 <= x <= n; for every x in S and every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), x != banned[i]; and sum_{x in S} x <= maxSum. Equivalently, there exists such a set S with |S| = r, and every such set T satisfies |T| <= r.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for the given banned, n, and maxSum.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= n.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r*(r+1)/2 <= maxSum.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there is no integer x such that 1 <= x <= n, x != banned[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), and x <= maxSum, then r = 0.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Let A be the set of integers x such that 1 <= x <= n and x != banned[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned). Whenever the function returns a result r, if sum_{x in A} x <= maxSum, then r = |A|.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), banned[i] < 1 or banned[i] > n, then r is the largest integer k such that 0 <= k <= n and k*(k+1)/2 <= maxSum.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Let a_1 < a_2 < ... < a_m be all integers x such that 1 <= x <= n and x != banned[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned). Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= m and, if r > 0, sum_{j=1}^{r} a_j <= maxSum.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every finite set T of integers such that every x in T satisfies 1 <= x <= n and x != banned[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), and sum_{x in T} x <= maxSum, we have |T| <= r.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Let a_1 < a_2 < ... < a_m be all integers x such that 1 <= x <= n and x != banned[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned). Whenever the function returns a result r, if r < m then sum_{j=1}^{r+1} a_j > maxSum.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: For every integer maxSum2 with maxSum <= maxSum2 <= 1000000000, if the function returns r on inputs (banned, n, maxSum) and returns r2 on inputs (banned, n, maxSum2), then r <= r2.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: For every integer n2 with n <= n2 <= 10000, if the function returns r on inputs (banned, n, maxSum) and returns r2 on inputs (banned, n2, maxSum), then r <= r2.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000.

statement: Suppose for every integer x with 1 <= x <= n, there exists i with 0 <= i < len(b1) and b1[i] = x if and only if there exists j with 0 <= j < len(b2) and b2[j] = x. If the function returns r1 on inputs (b1, n, maxSum) and returns r2 on inputs (b2, n, maxSum), then r1 = r2.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000; for both slices b1 and b2, 0 <= len(b1), len(b2) <= 10000 and every entry is between 1 and 10000.

statement: Let banned' be the slice of length len(banned)-1 such that banned'[k] = banned[k] for 0 <= k < j and banned'[k] = banned[k+1] for j <= k < len(banned)-1. If the function returns r on inputs (banned, n, maxSum) and returns r' on inputs (banned', n, maxSum), then r = r'.
preconditions: 0 <= len(banned) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(banned), 1 <= banned[i] <= 10000; 1 <= n <= 10000; 1 <= maxSum <= 1000000000; j is an index with 0 <= j < len(banned) and banned[j] > maxSum.
